topics.label: Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer course, outlines the learning objectives, and defines the scope of the lecture on the causes of cancer.

topics.label: Intrinsic and Inherited Drivers of Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics characterize cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease shaped by the microenvironment, intrinsic cellular processes, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore environmental carcinogens, the debate surrounding random bad luck versus external causes, and geographic and migration data linking environment to cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a paradigm of co-infection and translocation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical agents damage DNA directly or require endogenous metabolic activation to form mutagenic adducts.

topics.label: Tumour Promotion, Inflammation, and Cellular Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, tissue susceptibility, and developmental timing in driving malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for Determining and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic signatures, epidemiological surveys, biobanks, animal models, and in vitro assays used to evaluate whether an agent causes cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic summarizes the primary causes and challenges of evaluating carcinogens while framing exposure within everyday risk-versus-benefit decisions.
